cover.headline: Hey Missouri, don’t show me anymore!
cover.dek: The Tigers did not just beat Florida. They drove over it, backed up, drove over it again and then threw a couple touchdown passes just to make sure nobody mistook the afternoon for a competitive football game.

image.alt: Florida’s Emmanuel Oyebadejo (99) gets to Missouri quarterback Austin Simmons

damage.title: The damage
damage.dek: Florida came in scoring 53.5 points and gaining 532.8 yards a game. Missouri held the Gators to 17 and 325, and ran for 220 of its own.

more.label: By the Numbers: the full breakdown

flow.title: How the win slipped away
flow.dek: Florida’s chance to win, play by play. The Gators peaked at 80% in the first quarter and were level at 10-10 late in the second. Missouri scored the next 35.

marks.note: Florida’s high point, 9:52 left in the first quarter
Philo to Wilson ties it with 4:26 left in the half
Simmons to Goodie Sr.; Missouri leads the rest of the way
Roberts goes 80 yards with 13:33 to play

flow.summary: Line chart of Florida’s win probability against Missouri. It starts near 70%, peaks at 80% in the first quarter, dips below 50% in the second, climbs back to 64% at 10-10, falls to about 12% early in the third quarter and sits near zero through the fourth.

grades.title: Red ink in Columbia
grades.dek: Three Fs, and only one grade above a C.

items.note: “Starts with the coaching, starts with me.”

items.text: Embarrassing performance in every phase. Starts with the coaching, starts with me.
I take full accountability. I didn’t play my best game at all. Nobody did.
…tough teams stop the run, run the ball, and cover kicks.
